# buffers 0.1.1 license provenance

Author: James Halliday. The npm 0.1.1 package omits license metadata and a license file.
All six files in the locked npm package were compared byte-for-byte with upstream
commit 51ac8d0324008b0d0ed5759b1466402a77ff8dc8 and match exactly.
Its direct successor 1b745ee35d33eb166e15ef1866073a07c6d7de87, authored by
James Halliday, adds `MIT/X11` to package.json and README without changing code.
The original repository URL is unavailable; this exact upstream Git commit is
preserved in the BitPay fork:
https://github.com/bitpay/node-buffers/commit/1b745ee35d33eb166e15ef1866073a07c6d7de87

The license grant is therefore evidenced by the author's fixed commit for identical
source, rather than inferred from the parent's or another package's license.
Upstream's literal declaration is `MIT/X11`; no buffers source or installed package
is bundled in this source distribution. It remains separately licensed when installed.

Registry artifact:
https://registry.npmjs.org/buffers/-/buffers-0.1.1.tgz
Runtime index.js SHA-256:
97801e296ba5f3c32242f647e1daac5917e300367fed7935ab1e62f40adb1b8a

Debian's corresponding package records the same upstream grant and MIT license text:
https://sources.debian.org/copyright/license/node-buffers/0.1.1-2/

license grant by Closr):
